importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — A-frame, gable-roof resort cottage, glamping pod, and log cabin are visually distinct products that buyers identify by silhouette before reading any text. The product's primary appeal is aesthetic; buyers are purchasing a guest experience, and the cottage design IS the product differentiator.

Floor area, structure material, roof type, and room configuration are primary shortlisting criteria — buyers cannot evaluate project fit, cost, or regulatory compliance without these. Listings without specs cannot be shortlisted by resort developers or farmhouse operators.

Indian hospitality developers are cost-conscious and compare per-sq-ft rates across sellers, but price is only comparable after spec equivalence (material tier, floor area, furnishing level) is confirmed. Final price is always negotiated for custom or semi-custom projects; listed rate anchors the budget conversation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standardised glamping pods and compact single-room units are often quoted per piece (lump sum per unit); custom resort and farm cottages are quoted per sq ft of built-up area. Both conventions coexist in the market — unit must be shown alongside price to prevent misreading.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per piece is a documented market ambiguity in Indian modular cottage pricing. Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit — a per-piece quote for a 300 sq ft pod and a per-sq-ft quote for a 600 sq ft cottage are incomparable without unit clarity.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No established brand names with buyer recall exist in the Indian modular cottage market — buyers search by design type, material, and spec rather than manufacturer name; the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and turnkey contractors.
importance_ranking.reason: Post-sale dependency is high — buyers evaluate turnkey execution capability, installation track record, geographic service reach, and warranty support during vendor selection. Manufacturer status and project portfolio matter, but no dominant brand drives buyer preference.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — MS, bamboo, LGSF, and wood are non-interchangeable structural systems with a 3–5x price delta between budget bamboo and premium LGSF, making it the single largest price driver in this category.
Directly determines total project cost via per-sq-ft pricing — non-interchangeable across project requirements, and the primary scale variable that drives the overall contract value.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Thermal insulation specification (Rockwool, PIR, EPS, or none) is a primary quality and price tier separator for resort buyers in hill stations and coastal areas — PIR-insulated LGSF cottages command a significant premium over basic EPS or uninsulated structures.

Wall cladding system (sandwich panel, cement fibre board, FRP, or timber) determines durability, maintenance requirements, and aesthetic finish — a primary differentiator for resort developers evaluating long-term asset quality.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to manufacturers who work with that structural system — a bamboo specialist cannot supply an LGSF cottage, and a steel-frame fabricator cannot supply a log cabin; material is the primary supplier-capability filter.

Defines the spatial scope of the project — a single-room glamping pod and a 2BHK resort cottage are fundamentally different products requiring different design, material quantities, and manufacturing capability.

missing_important_specs.why_important: A-frame, gable-roof, flat-roof, and dome cottage styles are structurally distinct products — sellers specialise in specific roof forms, and buyers searching for an A-frame resort cottage cannot be served by a flat-roof portable cabin manufacturer.

Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires a bare structure, semi-furnished, or fully furnished turnkey cottage — the supply scope and project cost differ substantially, and not all manufacturers offer full interior fit-out.

buyer_spec_audit.image_upload_reason: Modular cottages have extreme design variation within the same spec combination — two wooden 1BHK cottages can look completely different in silhouette, facade treatment, and interior aesthetic. Resort developers and farmhouse owners typically have a specific design reference (competitor resort, Pinterest inspiration, architect sketch) they want to match. An uploaded reference image lets sellers identify whether their catalogue or custom design capability matches the buyer's vision, avoiding misaligned proposals.
